question: Q2: necessity of m9 - change it and recount the exact outcome (ops, time_log2, digest).
number: Change m9: to the constant 0 (word frozen, not part of the chain): 590 ops, -5 (-0.0121 bit); to 0x9e3779b9: 595 ops (0). Diffusion test (flip each of the 32 bits of m9, 48 random inputs each, 3 rounds): mean 128.1 of 256 digest bits change (per-bit means 125.7 to 131.8), and all 8 digest words change in every flip tested (8 flips per bit class sampled), so the word fully reaches the digest. Structural necessity (argued, NOT run): with m9 frozen the chain function lives on a smaller domain and a full 256-bit digest match then needs many partial collisions (for one frozen word about 2^32 collisions of a 224-bit function); at memory near 2^20 bytes the parallel-collision-search price per collision (about 2.5*sqrt(N/w), a literature formula applied by hand) is far above the saving. So the word stays variable; the op saving is not a lever on present knowledge.
notes: Tools first reproduced: 7-round empty-input vector af1349b9...f3262 and verifier blake3.py (rounds 1,2,3,5,7 on 40 random blocks each, 3-round 0^32||x on 100 inputs, all equal); traced circuit = 595 ops and time_log2 125.10856 (shipped), 0 mismatches vs scalar on 200 inputs. Variants traced and compared with the scalar function on 60 inputs (0 mismatches). The multi-collision cost is not tested by search.
